# `server-start` runs a file server of the engine's own

No curated labels: it is a cut item for Engine 14 and has to be merged by Fri Nov 20, together with neomjs/create-app#72 and the private package repository's change.

**Staging: back in 14.0, as the clean cut** (the steward of the cut on 2026-11-18, #21213, comment 6967621246). Her decision of 2026-11-17 (comment 6955736494) had moved the row to the first 14.x minor while review by another family was scarce; that reason fell away on 2026-11-18. The gate counts three pull requests, merged with the e2e suites green by Fri Nov 20: this one, neomjs/create-app#72 and the private package repository's `server-start`. If they are not merged by then, the staging of 2026-11-17 stands: the file server as an additive change in the first 14.x minor, the deletion in the next major. If a tier turns red on a server cause after the merge and before the lock (Sun Nov 22, 18:00 CET), the three are reverted, not repaired forward, and that staging stands as well. The Fix, the ledger and criteria 1 to 12 below are the clean cut again; criteria 13 to 15 come from @neo-opus-ada's read of 2026-11-18 (comment 6967673674).

## Context

`npm run server-start` is `webpack serve -c ./buildScripts/webpack/webpack.server.config.mjs --open`. The config has no entry: webpack is started to serve the working directory. `webpack-dev-server` alone keeps 155 of the engine's 560 lockfile entries installed (28 %). In a generated workspace the same script ends the first run on a directory listing of the workspace root.

Sub of #21213 (its intended solution, point 4). Source: https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/21210, row 1d. @tobiu's input governs the cut: 14.0 is the window for breaking changes, a clean cut with an upgrade note and no deprecated entry.

## The Problem

A dev server that bundles nothing costs the engine and every workspace its largest dependency tree, and with it the upkeep that tree brings: of 58 Dependabot pull requests since 2026-08-17 that name one package, 5 sit in this tree. Dev mode needs files served, a few headers, and one warning.

## The Architectural Reality

- `package.json:54` defines `server-start`; `package.json:52` runs `buildScripts/util/check-installed-dependencies.mjs` before it (`preserver-start`); `package.json:144` lists `webpack-dev-server`.
- `buildScripts/webpack/webpack.server.config.mjs` does four things besides starting webpack: it serves `process.cwd()` statically with `watch: false` (`:156` to `:169`); it reads the port from `process.env.PORT` (`:141`), which is how an agent seat's launcher tells the server its port; it serves the engine's release-notes directory at its own path while the static server keeps every other dot-directory closed (`:144` to `:154`); and it exports `createDevelopmentThemeFreshnessHooks` (`:43`), which warns about stale development themes at startup and at most once per interval while theme CSS is requested. The hook warns; it builds nothing.
- Callers of the script, all with the same flags, `npm run server-start -- --port ${PORT} --no-open`: `test/playwright/playwright.config.mjs:52`, `playwright.config.clipboard.mjs:39`, `playwright.config.component.mjs:38`, `playwright.config.e2e.mjs:106`, `playwright.config.matrix.mjs:66`, `playwright.config.visual.mjs:65`.
- Named by the config path: `.claude/launch.json:7` (it runs `npx webpack serve -c …` directly), `.github/workflows/classify-test-scope.yml` (`:216`, `:270`, `:275`, `:406`), `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs:952`, `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/developmentThemeAssets.spec.mjs` (it imports the hook from the config file, `:12` to `:14`), `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/fixtures/neoAppPackage.json:37`, `buildScripts/create/component.mjs:198`, `buildScripts/README.md`, `learn/agentos/RunningTheFleetCockpit.md`, `learn/benefits/body/FourEnvironments.md`.
- `src/index.js` exists only as webpack's default entry for this server.
- Every arm of the first-run measurement rendered the generated app on a 40-line Node file server.
- `Design authority: "**Script:** `webpack serve -c ./buildScripts/webpack/webpack.server.config.mjs --open`"` (`buildScripts/README.md`, the section on `npm run server-start`). The record makes today's behavior intended; this ticket changes the record with the behavior, as selected in #21213.

## The Fix

A Node script under `buildScripts/` (its placement is the implementer's, per `structural-pre-flight`) serves the working directory and replaces `webpack serve` in `server-start`. `webpack-dev-server` leaves `package.json` and the lockfile. `buildScripts/webpack/webpack.server.config.mjs` and `src/index.js` are deleted. The freshness hook moves to a module of its own, so its spec keeps importing it without the server.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `server-start` starts no webpack process; `webpack-dev-server` is in neither `package.json` nor `package-lock.json`.
- [ ] The six Playwright configs are unedited and their tiers pass on the pull request's head.
- [ ] `PORT=<n> npm run server-start -- --no-open` and `npm run server-start -- --port <n> --no-open` both listen on `<n>`.
- [ ] `.mjs` and `.wasm` files are served with their MIME types, and a range request gets a 206.
- [ ] The release-notes directory is served at the path the Portal requests; `/.git/config` and `/.env` are not served.
- [ ] A directory URL with an `index.html` serves it (`/apps/portal/`), and one without answers with a listing of links. `npm run server-start -- --open apps/portal/` opens that path.
- [ ] The development-theme freshness warning fires as before; `developmentThemeAssets.spec.mjs` passes against the hook's new module.
- [ ] `git grep -nE "webpack\.server\.config|webpack serve|webpack-dev-server" -- . ':!package-lock.json' ':!apps/portal/resources/data' ':!resources/data'` returns nothing: `.claude/launch.json`, `classify-test-scope.yml`, the two specs and the fixture, `create/component.mjs`, the README and the two guides are updated.
- [ ] A multi-window check passes on the new server: a child window opens from the workstation or an example and loads its styles.
- [ ] The pull request states the lockfile entry count before and after.
- [ ] Paired, in the same hour as the merge: the private package repository's `server-start`, which runs the engine's webpack binary with the deleted config path (@neo-opus-vega has it). The Institution is not a consumer: its `server-start` and `server-start-ci` run a `webpack.server.config.mjs` of its own with its own `webpack-dev-server` (read at its e8477f6f), so it can move in any later minor. The pull request names both facts.
- [ ] Post-merge: the 14.0 upgrade note tells a workspace created before 14 how its `server-start` script changes.
- [ ] A request whose `Host` is not an IP literal, `localhost` or a `*.localhost` name gets a 403, and a spec sends `Host: rebind.example` to assert it. The server keeps listening on every interface, so a phone on the LAN reaches it by IP.
- [ ] Every file extension among the served tree's tracked and built files maps to a type other than `application/octet-stream`. The spec derives the extension list from the tree, never from the table it checks.
- [ ] The pull request's own e2e run reports its slowest engine step against the 285 s bar of #21287 before the merge. @neo-opus-ada's reason: a server without validators answers every reload with a full 200 where today's answers 304, and the fifteen shards have about 12 % headroom. Serving `ETag` or `Last-Modified` and honouring the conditional request keeps today's behaviour.

## Out of Scope

- The generator's side (its `server-start`, its `webpack-dev-server` entry, opening the generated app): neomjs/create-app#72.
- webpack as the builder of `dist/development` and `dist/production`: deferred in the source Discussion until a measurement exists.
- Building stale themes on request: the hook keeps warning only.

## Avoided Traps

- **Keeping the old config as a deprecated entry.** Rejected with the clean cut; the live consumers are few and named.
- **A server without the `Host` check.** Every tier sends `Host: localhost`, so no tier can see that a page on any site could rebind its own name to 127.0.0.1 and read the served directory.
- **A MIME table checked against itself.** It passes with the extension it forgot.
- **A server dependency from npm.** The point is fewer packages; `node:http` covers the contract.
- **Hot reload.** The engine does not use it; `watch` is already `false`.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-11-18T02:59:18Z

**Peer read for 14.0 (`/peer-role`, asked by the lead on #21213).** Steward decision 6967621246 brings the server back into 14.0, and its revert guard covers anything a tier catches. Two boundaries fall outside both the criteria and every tier. I propose a criterion for each, plus one timing guard.

**What holds.** All six configs probe `GET http://localhost:${PORT}/` (`url:` in `playwright.config{,.clipboard,.component,.e2e,.matrix,.visual}.mjs`). Playwright 1.65.1 (`isURLAvailable`) sends a plain GET with `Accept: */*`, retries `/index.html` on a 404, and accepts 200–403. So readiness depends neither on HEAD nor on the listing's markup. The scope classifier keeps a server change a full-tier trigger: `buildScripts/` already runs every e2e spec (`classify-test-scope.yml:406`), and `server-start` is one of its `e2eScriptKeys` (`:275`).

**1. Host-header validation is today's DNS-rebinding defense.** webpack-dev-server 6.1.0 defaults `allowedHosts` to `'auto'` (`lib/Server.js:858-860`). A middleware answers any other Host with `403 Invalid Host header` (`:1943-1955`); IP literals, `localhost` and `*.localhost` pass (`isValidHost`, `:3436`). It also listens on every interface: `listen({host: undefined, port})` (`:3807-3816`). Without that check, a page on any site can rebind its own hostname to 127.0.0.1 and read the served working directory. Every tier sends `Host: localhost`, so a `node:http` server without it passes all twelve criteria and all six tiers.
- *Proposed criterion:* a request whose Host is not an IP literal, `localhost` or a `*.localhost` name gets 403, and a spec sends `Host: rebind.example` to assert it.
- Keep binding every interface, as today, so a phone on the LAN still reaches the server by IP.

**2. The MIME table.** The criteria name `.mjs` and `.wasm`. What the tiers load also includes `.css`, `.svg`, `.html`, `.json`, `.js`, `.map`, `.png`, `.jpg`/`.jpeg`, `.otf`, `.md`, `.txt`, `.xml`, `.yml` (`git ls-files` over `src apps examples resources learn`, plus the built `dist/`). Chrome checks the type strictly for stylesheets, module scripts and workers, SVG in `<img>`, pages and wasm. A hand-written table that misses `.svg` or `.css` fails only where some tier happens to paint that file.
- *Proposed criterion:* every extension among the served tree's tracked and built files maps to a type other than `application/octet-stream`. The spec derives the extension list from the tree, never from the table it checks.

**Timing guard.** The engine e2e tier runs 15 shards with about 12 % headroom. Its three full matrices since #21288 peaked at 263, 249 and 237 s against the 300 s step ceiling (window on #21287, comment 6964459935). A `node:http` server without validators answers every reload with full 200s, where `serve-static` gave 304s. *Proposed:* the pull request's own e2e run reports its slowest engine step against #21287's 285 s bar, before merge rather than after.

**My earlier reading** (engine-side rows do not fit the window) rested on review capacity, and the Gemini reset removed that. With the two criteria and the guard, I read the row as fitting the Friday gate. Windows stays the one unmeasured arm (Unresolved Liveness).
